summary.title: Data Structure Visualizations
summary.one_liner: An index of interactive animations showing how common data structures and algorithms (stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, sorting, graph search, and more) work step by step.
keywords: how does a data structure work
takeaways: Lists of visualizations covering basic structures (stacks, queues, lists), search trees (BST, AVL, red-black, splay, B and B+ trees), and hash tables
Sorting animations include bubble, selection, insertion, shell, merge, quick, bucket, counting, radix, and heap sort
Graph algorithms covered include BFS, DFS, connected components, Dijkstra, Prim, Kruskal, topological sort, and Floyd-Warshall
Some visualizations (lists, Huffman coding) are noted as available only in the Java version
Geometric transformation matrices (2D and 3D rotation, scale, translation, coordinate changes) are also included
summary.summary: This page is a navigation index of interactive data structure and algorithm visualizations hosted by USF (Galles). The listing groups topics into basics, search trees, hash tables, sorting, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, geometric algorithms, disjoint sets, and Huffman coding. Each entry links to an animation that shows the operations step by step. The page text itself gives only topic names, so the specific details of each animation are not visible from this text.
